gen_risks.description: Inaccurate or low‑quality data in the NPR due to integration of multiple legacy databases.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement rigorous data cleaning, validation rules and continuous quality monitoring during enrollment and updates.
gen_risks.evidence: Existing databases had inconsistent quality and data formats, likely leading to substantial inaccuracies (Section 11).

gen_risks.description: Failure or delays in the biometric solution for NPR enrollment and authentication.
gen_risks.mitigation: Secure long‑term maintenance contracts, conduct regular system testing, and keep backup hardware/software components.
gen_risks.evidence: Design, supply, commissioning, and maintenance of the biometric solution of the NPR (Table 80).

gen_risks.description: Generation of e‑waste from mobile units and ICT equipment with improper disposal.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce the MoI e‑waste management procedure, partner with certified recyclers, and train staff on disposal protocols.
gen_risks.evidence: Risks associated with the use of electronic devices (such as mobile units) include the potential generation of e‑waste and its improper disposal (Section 85).

gen_risks.description: Inadequate Error, Fraud and Corruption (EFC) monitoring leading to leakage or fraud.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop and operationalize a robust end‑to‑end EFC monitoring system with regular audits and whistle‑blower channels.
gen_risks.evidence: Design and develop an end‑to‑end Error, Fraud, and Corruption (EFC) monitoring system (Section 30).

gen_risks.description: Reliance on Excel spreadsheets for financial reporting may cause data quality and timeliness issues.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt dedicated financial management software and provide staff training on its use.
gen_risks.evidence: Use of a spreadsheet “Excel” may lead to challenges in quality and timeliness of IFRs (Section 69).

gen_risks.description: Duplication or overlap of expenditures due to the same budget line (AMO‑TADAMON) being used for multiple programs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement clear budget coding, cross‑check allocations, and conduct periodic audit reviews.
gen_risks.evidence: Risk of duplication or overlap due to the use of the same budget line “AMO‑TADAMON” (Section 69).

gen_risks.description: Retroactive financing limit (20 % of loan) may be insufficient to cover eligible past expenditures.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prioritize retroactive claims, seek additional donor support if gaps remain, and align expenditures with the cap early.
gen_risks.evidence: Retroactive financing up to 20 % of the World Bank loan amount is available (Section 74).

gen_risks.description: Delay in achieving the NPR coverage target of >60 % of the population by end‑2024.
gen_risks.mitigation: Monitor enrollment rates monthly, allocate extra resources to remote areas, and adjust outreach tactics as needed.
gen_risks.evidence: The NPR national rollout aims to expand coverage to more than 60 % of the total population by the end of 2024 (Section 32).

gen_risks.description: Operationalization of the NRA may be delayed, hindering coordinated management of NPR and SR.
gen_risks.mitigation: Fast‑track recruitment, define clear governance procedures, and provide capacity‑building support to NRA staff.
gen_risks.evidence: The NRA operationalization will be essential to ensuring that the initiative and project efforts are sustainable (Section 27).

gen_risks.description: Delay in completing the SR process evaluation and manual validation required for PBCs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Assign a dedicated team with fixed deadlines and integrate evaluation milestones into the overall project schedule.
gen_risks.evidence: Process evaluation of the SR and development of the procedures manual are required (Sections 38‑39).

gen_risks.description: Exclusion of vulnerable groups due to inefficient or inadequate public communication and outreach.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement the Stakeholder Engagement Plan with multi‑channel outreach, monitor enrollment gaps, and adjust messaging promptly.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential negative social impacts related to exclusion of vulnerable groups due to inefficient communication (Section 85).

gen_risks.description: Informal‑sector workers may resist providing personal data, limiting enrollment.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct targeted awareness campaigns emphasizing privacy safeguards and the non‑taxation purpose of data collection.
gen_risks.evidence: Workers in the informal sector are wary of providing their information to the government (Section 53).

gen_risks.description: Data‑privacy breach or non‑compliance with Moroccan data‑protection law (Law 09‑08).
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply privacy‑by‑design, conduct regular security audits, and enforce strict access controls per Law 09‑08.
gen_risks.evidence: Mitigation measures related to data privacy and protection follow national regulations (Law 09‑08) (Section 87).

gen_risks.description: Changes in legal or environmental‑social frameworks could render project activities non‑compliant.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain continuous legal review, update procedures as needed, and engage the World Bank’s legal advisors early.
gen_risks.evidence: The project will rely on the Borrower’s ESF to comply with ESS2 requirements (Section 88).

gen_risks.description: Climate‑related shocks (droughts, floods) could increase vulnerability of target households, affecting project outcomes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate climate‑risk data into targeting algorithms and design flexible emergency response mechanisms.
gen_risks.evidence: Climate‑related shocks, primarily droughts, represent significant risks to the Moroccan economy (Section 3).

gen_risks.description: MoI and PMU capacity may be strained by rapid expansion of NPR/SR, affecting implementation quality.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen institutional capacity through the Center of Excellence, targeted training, and additional technical assistance.
gen_risks.evidence: Rapid expansion has strained the government’s and the MoI’s capacity to operationalize the NRA (Section 52).

gen_risks.description: Macroeconomic shocks (inflation, recession) could reduce fiscal space for government contributions to social programs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain fiscal buffers, explore flexible financing arrangements, and adjust program design to cost‑effective delivery.
gen_risks.evidence: The 2022 inflationary terms‑of‑trade shock led to fluctuations in GDP growth and slowdown of economic recovery (Section 3).

gen_risks.description: Coordination challenges with the EU on communication and fraud‑management components may cause delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish regular joint coordination meetings, shared work plans, and clear points of contact.
gen_risks.evidence: The EU is collaborating with Morocco’s MoI on communication aspects and the first version of the fraud management system (Section 51).

gt_risks.description: Stakeholder risk is assessed as Substantial. Given the complex nature of the operation and the involvement of multiple stakeholders in the implementation of the National Population Register (NPR) and the Social Registry (SR), the Project Management Unit (PMU) will need to put considerable effort into ensuring better coordination to achieve the PDO. The national rollout and the improvement of the NPR and the SR will need strong stakeholder engagement, including citizens concerned by social protection programs who are often poor and vulnerable.
gt_risks.mitigation: The communication strategy will continue to inform all stakeholders involved in project implementation and will capitalize on lessons learned from the first Identity and Targeting for Social Protection project (P155198). The PMU envisions improving the grievance mechanism at local and national levels and establishing a system to promote citizen engagement and transparency. The Inter-Ministerial Steering Committee is responsible for developing guidelines for the strategic policy for the envisaged reform and ensuring a link with the ongoing social protection reform. Technical work will also cover a process evaluation to identify challenges, propose remedies, and provide recommendations to enhance system implementation at central and local levels.
